title: Cauliflower Mac and Cheese
subtitle: Macaroni and cauliflower in a double-cheddar sauce with a crunchy breadcrumb top
excerpt: Cauliflower mac and cheese is macaroni and cauliflower florets baked in a rich cheddar sauce with a crisp breadcrumb and cheese topping. The cauliflower softens in the oven and absorbs the sauce while the top browns and crisps. It is a more substantial version of macaroni cheese and works as a main course.
sourceNotes: Cauliflower cheese is a Victorian British side dish staple documented in Mrs Beeton, Book of Household Management (1861), Project Gutenberg #10136. The combination with macaroni became popular in British home cooking in the twentieth century as a way to make macaroni cheese more substantial.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze before baking. Thaw overnight and bake from cold, adding 10 minutes to the time.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Assemble up to a day ahead and refrigerate unbaked. Add 10 minutes to the bake time if cooking from cold.

content.text: Cauliflower mac and cheese adds a head of cauliflower to classic macaroni cheese, giving the dish more substance and a slightly sweet, nutty note from the roasted cauliflower that contrasts with the sharpness of the cheddar sauce. The breadcrumb topping adds a crunch layer that plain macaroni cheese lacks. Both pasta and cauliflower are par-cooked before baking; the oven finishes the cooking and forms the crust.

Heat the oven to 200°C (fan 180°C / gas mark 6). Bring a large pot of salted water to the boil. Cook {{macaroni}} of macaroni for 2 minutes less than the packet instructions. Add {{cauliflower}} of cauliflower florets for the last 3 minutes. Drain together and set aside.

Melt {{unsalted-butter}} of butter in a saucepan over a medium heat. Add {{plain-flour}} of flour and stir for 2 minutes. Remove from the heat and gradually whisk in {{whole-milk}} of milk. Return to the heat, stirring constantly, and cook for 4 to 5 minutes until the sauce thickens. Remove from the heat and stir in 200 g of the grated cheddar, the {{english-mustard}} of mustard, the nutmeg, and the salt. Stir until the cheese melts completely.
Add the drained pasta and cauliflower to the cheese sauce and stir gently to combine. Pour into a large baking dish.

Mix {{breadcrumbs-dried}} of breadcrumbs with the remaining 60 g of grated cheddar and scatter evenly over the top of the dish. Bake for 20 to 25 minutes until the topping is golden and the sauce is bubbling at the edges. Rest for 5 minutes before serving.

items.cause: The cauliflower was cooked too long before baking.
items.fix: Add the cauliflower for only the last 3 minutes of the pasta cooking time. It should be tender but still have some resistance. It finishes cooking in the oven.

items.symptom: The sauce is grainy or broken
items.cause: The cheese was added while the sauce was still on a high heat, or a very low-fat cheese was used.
items.fix: Remove the sauce from the heat before stirring in the cheese. A mature cheddar with a good fat content melts smoothly; reduced-fat cheeses are more prone to splitting.

items.cause: The oven was not hot enough, or the dish was too full and created steam.
items.fix: Ensure the oven is properly preheated to 200°C. Scatter the crumbs in an even layer and do not pack them. Switch to the grill for the last 2 minutes if the top needs more colour.

content.text: Cauliflower cheese is a traditional British side dish that has been on dinner tables since at least the Victorian era. Adding macaroni makes it a main course. The two dishes share the same béchamel-and-cheddar base and bake in the same way; the combination is a pragmatic British solution to feeding a family from a single dish. The mustard in the sauce is the trick: it lifts the flavour of the cheddar without making the dish taste mustardy.
